test_title: SSC Selection Post 2025 (Graduate Level) Official Paper (Held On: 26 Jul, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question:
Match the following Articles with their provisions:

A. Article 50 1. Original jurisdiction of Supreme Court

B. Article 131 2. Separation of Judiciary from Executive

C. Article 312 3. Creation of All India Services

D. Article 263 4. Inter-State Council
solution:
The correct answer is __**A - 2, B - 1, C - 3, D - 4**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 50 - Separation of Judiciary from Executive**:

 
 
• **Article 50** is a part of the **Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP)** under **Part IV** of the **Constitution of India**.
 
• It mandates that the **State** shall take steps to separate the **judiciary** from the **executive** in the public services of the State to ensure **judicial independence**.
 
• The separation is vital for the **Rule of Law** and to prevent the interference of the executive in the administration of justice. *Hence, the match A-2 is correct.*
 
 
 
• **Article 131 - Original Jurisdiction of the Supreme Court**:
 
 
• **Article 131** deals with the **Original Jurisdiction** of the **Supreme Court of India**, meaning cases that can be brought directly to the Supreme Court.
 
• This jurisdiction covers **federal disputes** such as those between the **Government of India** and one or more **States**, or between two or more **States**.
 
• It serves as the mechanism for resolving legal conflicts involving the **units of the Indian federation**. *Hence, the match B-1 is correct.*
 
 
 
• **Article 312 - All India Services**:
 
 
• **Article 312** empowers the **Parliament of India** to create **All India Services** common to both the **Union** and the **States**.
 
• A new **All India Service** can be created only if the **Rajya Sabha** passes a resolution supported by not less than **two-thirds** of the members present and voting.
 
• Currently, there are three All India Services: **Indian Administrative Service (IAS)**, **Indian Police Service (IPS)**, and **Indian Forest Service (IFoS)**. *Hence, the match C-3 is correct.*
 
 
 
• **Article 263 - Inter-State Council**:
 
 
• **Article 263** provides for the establishment of an **Inter-State Council** to investigate and discuss subjects of common interest between the **Union** and the **States**.
 
• The **President of India** is authorized to establish this council by an **Executive Order** if it appears that the **public interest** would be served.
 
• The primary function of the council is to promote **cooperative federalism** and ensure better **coordination** of policy and action. *Hence, the match D-4 is correct.*
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Federalism and Article 131**:

 
 
• The **Original Jurisdiction** excludes disputes arising out of any **pre-Constitution treaty**, agreement, or covenant.
 
• In **1977**, in the case of **State of Rajasthan v. Union of India**, the scope of **Article 131** was extensively discussed regarding the **President's power** to dissolve State Assemblies.
 
 
 
• **History of All India Services (Article 312)**:
 
 
• The **Indian Forest Service** was the third service added to the list of All India Services in the year **1966** under the **All India Services Act, 1951**.
 
• The **Rajya Sabha** holds special power under **Article 312**, which reflects the **federal character** of the Indian Constitution as it represents the interests of the **States**.
 
 
 
• **Evolution of Inter-State Council (Article 263)**:
 
 
• The **Sarkaria Commission (1983-1988)** strongly recommended the establishment of a permanent **Inter-State Council**.
 
• Following these recommendations, the **Inter-State Council** was finally established by a **Presidential Order** on **28th May 1990**.
 
• The **Prime Minister** acts as the **Chairman** of the Council, while **Chief Ministers** of all States and **Union Territories** are its members.
 
 
 
• **DPSP and Judicial Independence**:
 
 
• While **Article 50** is a **Directive Principle** (and thus non-justiciable), it influenced the **Criminal Procedure Code (CrPC), 1973**, which effectively separated the **judicial functions** from **executive magistrates** at the district level.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Summary of Articles**:

 
 
• **Article 50**: Promotes the **separation of powers** between the executive and judiciary.
 
• **Article 131**: Provides a legal forum for **Inter-State** and **Center-State** disputes.
 
• **Article 312**: Highlights the unique legislative power of the **Upper House (Rajya Sabha)**.
 
• **Article 263**: Acts as a bridge for **administrative and political cooperation** in a federal setup.
